evidence_used: flat, parallel sides of the box providing good contact area
calculation_summary: Estimated base gripping force for a moderately weighted small cardboard box (~0.3-0.5 kg) using high-friction silicone pads: F = weight / (2 * mu). Assuming an effective friction coefficient around 0.5-0.6 and a safety factor for smooth cardboard, resulting in roughly 4.5 N normal force.
assumptions_and_uncertainty: Exact object mass is unmeasured and visually estimated from object size.
Surface friction coefficient is assumed based on standard dry cardboard-silicone interaction.
Visual approximation introduces uncertainty in weight and center of mass.
reasoning_trace: The query object is a small cardboard box containing poker chips. The silicone gripper features high-friction pads well-suited to grip dry cardboard surfaces. Given the flat rectangular geometry of the box, optimal parallel-jaw contact can be achieved across a sufficient surface area. Without authoritative mass measurements, the required force is estimated visually based on standard object scale and typical weight for a box of poker chips, yielding a predicted stationary-finger normal force of 4.5 N to securely lift and hold the object against gravity.
